title: Seek Wisdom
coreMove: Wisdom is not more input; it is the practiced sort that joins knowledge, experience, and prudence so pressure does not pick what matters for you.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers handling quick service pressure with too many facts at once
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small rush can turn knowledge into noise unless judgment orders it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A close food-truck moment shows knowledge, experience, and prudence working without a formal decision speech.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers reviewing a choice after the outcome is already known
exampleSpecs.stakes: old experience may explain a failure without excusing the judgment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The garden result is known first; Ryan reconstructs how knowledge, experience, and prudence should have worked.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers who keep gathering one more detail while the real issue continues
exampleSpecs.stakes: a familiar maintenance habit can hide a new risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Isidore notices his own error while cleaning the lint screen and redirects attention.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers tempted to turn old wisdom into quotes instead of conduct
exampleSpecs.stakes: tradition can become decoration unless it changes how a person handles friction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A coat-check memo carries the scene and uses Stoicism, Buddhism, and Christianity as conduct training.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers comparing expertise that rushes with judgment that sorts
exampleSpecs.stakes: one intake response can mistake speed for wisdom
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Constance and Davinder handle the same intake pressure in opposite ways, with different results.

exampleSpecs.audience: Readers who collect wise language before choosing a concrete action
exampleSpecs.stakes: old teaching must help choose a proportional load, not decorate indecision
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A mentor reframes Monique's stuck view at the gym equipment cage with a quotable line.
